decisions.statement: A unit is written from a page's value and the path that page is at.
A service stating a schedule is written a timer beside its unit.
Only the timer of a scheduled service is installed.
A service stating no schedule is wanted by the target that service states or by the default target.
A service stating no schedule is started again when the service stops.
A command that fails fails the unit.
A service stating that service needs secrets is handed those secrets by the shell its unit starts.
A service that cannot read those secrets leaves rather than starting without them.
The exit that leaving is is not one the unit counts as a success.
A service leaving on that exit is not started again, since nothing it does mends it.
A service reaching here has its command lines settled already.
A service is put in the slice holding the work that ranks below Alan's apps.
Nothing here reads a file.
Nothing here runs systemctl.
Nothing here settles where a unit is installed.
Every option a service's page states reaches that service's unit or timer.
One exit means a service is leaving for code that moved rather than leaving because it failed.
That exit is named here, and every service stating no schedule recycles on it.
A scheduled service recycles on nothing, its next tick reading the code as it is.
A unit ending on the signal that asks it to stop is a clean stop rather than a failure.
A scheduled service names that clean stop as a service stating no schedule does.
An exit code a service states joins that exit rather than replacing it.
A unit the loader starts is ordered after the pages service and wants it.
Every unit runs its command in the checkout, so a bare specifier resolves there.
A unit is given the origin the pages service answers on where one is handed in.
The name that origin is given is the one the caller of the pages reads.
A service handed no origin has that name nowhere in its unit.

definition: the unit and timer text a workstation service's page states
